policies.statement: Immediately after receiving a new-project name, ask what the product should actually do and invite a detailed natural-language project/manifest description, explaining that Codex will proactively structure it, challenge gaps, and that the generated project can refine it later. Store a supplied description only as an intake draft, never as active modules. On the generated project's first interaction, inspect and evaluate any draft or filled manifest, explain the successive Project Definition Intake up front, identify strengths, gaps, and contradictions, and ask whether to refine it further or—when decision-ready—begin from the confirmed scope; an empty or materially incomplete definition continues the focused interview before dependent implementation.
policies.projectionStatement: A new project asks immediately for a detailed natural-language project/manifest description and explains Codex's guided, refinable Project Definition Intake. A pending or incomplete manifest triggers evaluation and focused questions before dependent implementation; drafts never invent active modules.

policies.statement: `docs/project.md` is a current-state inventory, never a roadmap: active modules must exist and be integrated, while confirmed unimplemented candidates live only in `docs/future-modules.md` and move into the manifest in the same change that implements them. A newly voiced idea is not implementation authorization; ambiguous intent must be clarified and remains non-authorizing future intent until the developer explicitly chooses current implementation.
policies.projectionStatement: `docs/project.md` is a current-state inventory, never a roadmap; unimplemented candidates live in `docs/future-modules.md` and move in the implementation change. A newly voiced idea is not implementation authorization; clarify ambiguity and treat it as future intent meanwhile.

policies.statement: Documentation remains fully inspectable but has one canonical owner per concern: root `AGENTS.md` is an always-loaded safe-entry bootstrap capped at 24 KiB, `instructions.md` owns complete workflow policy, the README owns human setup/use, `docs/project.md` owns current implemented reality, `docs/future-modules.md` owns only confirmed deferred candidates, and focused documents require a distinct audience and maintenance owner. Secondary surfaces link and summarize instead of duplicating normative detail, while skills use progressive disclosure and load their full workflow only when relevant. Larger model context windows never justify repeated policy or stale documentation; completed-goal housekeeping and `docs:check` enforce bootstrap size, meaningful unique headings, valid references, and canonical-owner separation without hiding framework elements. Skills retain specialized procedures and reference the existing canonical workflow instead of repeating admission, coordination, capacity and publication rules. Required native projections are derived views, not additional authorities. Native skill activation defaults to implicit invocation; an explicitly chosen explicit-only skill may set boolean policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false. General discovery remains manifest-led exact search in instructions, not a separate skill. Material skill changes use bounded realistic trigger and authority scenarios, without claiming model obedience from static checks or adding another evaluation runtime.
policies.projectionStatement: Keep framework elements inspectable with one canonical owner per concern: `AGENTS.md` is the always-loaded safe-entry bootstrap capped at 24 KiB, full policy stays in `instructions.md`, and skills load progressively. Secondary surfaces summarize and link; larger contexts never justify duplicated or stale policy. Keep skills procedure-specific and reference canonical workflow rather than copying governance. Discovery lives in instructions; native explicit-only activation is supported when selected. Validate material skill changes with bounded scenarios and state evidence limits.

policies.statement: Never implement a material change as a quick fix, symptom patch, local workaround, or first-plausible solution. Before writing, reconstruct the relevant system, identify the root cause and canonical owner, trace contracts and consumers, compare viable designs in whole-project context, and research current primary, official, or peer-reviewed evidence whenever it could materially change the choice. Choose the best-supported durable solution within authorized scope; speed, token pressure, failing checks, and urgent Dev feedback never lower the standard. A temporary mitigation requires explicit user authorization or immediate safety containment, bounded risk and a removal condition, and durable follow-up; Dev stays fast through a sound early artifact and isolated parallel or deferred verification, not structural debt or weakened contracts. Before additional research, abstraction, hardening, tests, documentation, cleanup or optimization, identify the approved user outcome, acceptance blocker or plausible material risk it improves. Omit work that changes none; best-supported means fit for purpose, not maximum depth, and sufficient evidence returns work to the highest-value unfinished step without waiving material risks.
policies.projectionStatement: Never use a quick fix, symptom patch, or first-plausible implementation for material work. Establish root cause and owner, compare viable designs in whole-project context, research when evidence could change the choice, and implement the best-supported durable solution. Dev speed comes from parallel or deferred verification, never lower engineering quality. Extra work must improve an approved outcome, acceptance blocker or material risk; omit speculative expansion.

policies.statement: CodexRig and every generated project run exactly one current internal contract per concern. When an owned contract changes, migrate every owned durable and mutable state representation plus all producers and consumers in the same coherent change, then delete superseded schemas, readers, writers, aliases, shims, fallback branches, paths, flags, tests, and documentation; never dual-read, dual-write, or retain dormant compatibility code. Robustness, resilience, fault tolerance, and lightweight operation come from strict current-schema validation, parent-bound atomic transitions, bounded recovery, idempotent repair, and fail-closed handling of corrupt or mechanically indeterminate current state, not parallel interpreters. No runtime, reset, or framework-upgrade path interprets a superseded internal schema.
policies.projectionStatement: Retain exactly one current internal contract per concern: migrate owned state and every consumer together, then remove superseded schemas, shims, fallback branches, paths, tests, and documentation. Robustness and lightweight fault tolerance come from atomic current-schema validation, bounded recovery, and fail-closed indeterminate state; no runtime, reset, or framework-upgrade path interprets a superseded schema.

policies.statement: Local Codex memory isolation is repository- and worktree-root-bound in ignored root CODEX_HOME entries; private framework coordination alone stays under `.codex/runtime/`; generated projects receive no framework or sibling runtime or memory state and use memories only inside their own clean runtime home. Canonical start runs `codex update` first and stops on failure, validates the prepared locked toolchain, compatible dependencies, and local framework evidence, then opens native `codex resume` with repository-root CODEX_HOME and explicit --cd; tool installation, dependency refresh, and online framework diagnosis remain separate maintenance actions. Only --no-alt-screen and explicit Dev-only --yolo are launcher controls; prompts are entered after selection. Before admission, the controller binds canonical Node.js, Codex, pnpm, and hook-shell executables to absolute paths outside the writable root, captures the startup basis, reserves native selection in an exclusive launcher lease, and issues the bound attestation. Before Codex consumes ignored root `config.toml`, only private non-executable repository trust, prior hook state, notice state, approval routing, service-tier metadata, typed terminal preferences, and bounded Codex-persisted model/reasoning preferences are permitted; tracked project config remains the model/reasoning source of truth and the controller projects its exact values into every fresh or resumed Codex CLI launch; `notify`, MCP, plugin, provider, and unknown configuration blocks startup, with revalidation before the real launch. While holding the reservation, the controller injects exactly one SessionStart and one Stop definition through session-only CLI configuration, forces the external hook shell through the sanitized child environment, and requires the same Codex executable's stable `hooks/list` inventory to contain exactly those two enabled, trusted controller hashes without warnings. Tracked `.codex/hooks.json` executes nothing, no global hook-trust bypass is used, and every additional user, project-file, or plugin hook blocks startup. Only after that proof does the controller bind a gated preloaded supervisor, persist the spawn handoff, open the gate, and bind the exact Codex child PID in the current schema-6 lease. Only the exact registered controller may mutate the lease. Release requires it to authenticate the supervisor's terminal child-exit proof against the private issue-time gate secret and persist the terminal `completed` phase first; a normal wrapper exit code alone is insufficient. A private parent-liveness pipe makes a controller crash terminate and reap the child; a killed supervisor cannot hide the separately recorded child, and a crash before PID binding remains an ownership-confirmation blocker. The short-lived writer lease remains separate from the latest verified Codex session marker and live while its controller, supervisor, exact Codex process, or handoff is active or indeterminate. A valid active-phase lease whose complete recorded process set is mechanically proven dead repairs missing or invalid recovery before cleanup while retaining any different valid marker; namespace or other process uncertainty is never proof of death. Authenticated SessionStart binds the actual user-selected session ID. Picker cancellation releases the pending lease without creating session/recovery state; failed selection never triggers an automatic fresh fallback. Full reset never interprets a non-current lease; after it holds the lifecycle lock and proves repository-wide runtime quiescence, it discards incompatible private runtime as disposable state. SessionStart changes no tracked source or external state and binds only private lease/recovery state after validating the effective model and permission mode.
policies.projectionStatement: Keep local Codex state in ignored repository-root CODEX_HOME entries and private framework coordination under `.codex/runtime/`; generated projects receive no source or sibling runtime. Canonical start runs `codex update` first, stops on failure, validates prepared tools/dependencies, then opens native `codex resume` with root CODEX_HOME and explicit --cd. Enter prompts after native selection. The preloaded controller binds external executables, permits only typed non-executable ignored runtime metadata and Codex-persisted model/reasoning preferences beneath tracked project policy, projects that exact policy into every fresh or resumed Codex CLI launch, and requires exactly two trusted session-only hooks through stable `hooks/list`, with no additional hook or global bypass. One schema-6 lease records controller, gated supervisor, durable handoff, and exact Codex PID; only the exact controller mutates it, and authenticated terminal proof must persist `completed` before release. Crash uncertainty stays blocked, latest-session recovery remains separate, and native selection binds only at authenticated SessionStart; cancellation creates no session record and failed selection never triggers automatic fallback. Full reset discards non-current private runtime only after lifecycle locking and repository-wide quiescence, without interpreting another schema. SessionStart mutates only private lease/recovery state.

policies.statement: At every primary Codex startup or resume in a generated project, before intake-dependent implementation or a new slice, perform a complete Startup Repository Reconstruction: read bootstrap/instructions/README, the current manifest and optional bounded work state; inventory active source roots, domains/modules/surfaces, public contracts, owned data, configuration, delivery state, dependencies, tests/verifiers, documentation, composition, the root's Git/Git-less/inconsistent classification, Git status/diff/branch/upstream, available task branches, every same-clone worktree, writer-lease state, each safe latest-session recovery marker, and safe verification evidence. Use exact search and direct source inspection to trace representative relationships without blindly loading every file or private Codex transcripts. Within the one-host/one-developer model, every visible same-host project change is developer-owned main-stream input regardless of Codex account; process control remains provenance-bound. Invoke `$resume-project` for unfinished work, automatically continue the unique coherent stream, safely integrate or consolidate only unambiguous residue, use `$system-coherence` for material drift, rerun affected evidence and the course check, and only then begin a new slice or pending-manifest intake. Preserve active writers, unrelated state, and incompatible ambiguity; ask one focused content question only when current evidence cannot choose. Inventory isolates per-root inconsistency so stale or malformed siblings do not suppress safe reconstruction or mechanically independent cleanup; live or indeterminate competing writers, unsafe bindings, and content ambiguity block only affected writes/publication. Current files/commands outrank memory, resumed transcript context, or a quiet Git view.
policies.projectionStatement: Startup Repository Reconstruction runs at every primary startup/resume: inspect manifest/work state, roots/modules/surfaces/contracts/config/tests/docs/composition, Git/Git-less root kind, upstream/task branches, every same-clone worktree, writer lease, latest safe session marker, and verification evidence with exact search and source inspection. One host's visible project changes are developer-owned regardless of Codex account, while process control stays provenance-bound. Per-root inconsistencies remain visible without suppressing safe reconstruction; only unsafe or ambiguous affected writes/publication wait. Automatically continue the unique coherent unfinished stream; preserve active writers and genuine ambiguity, asking only when evidence cannot choose.

policies.statement: Root `src/` is the default Product Root; non-trivial product code starts as a modular monolith with cohesive replaceable modules, narrow public contracts, private internals, owned data and migrations, explicit acyclic dependencies, focused verifiers, and assembled-system evidence.
policies.projectionStatement: Root `src/` is the default Product Root; non-trivial product code starts as a modular monolith with cohesive replaceable modules, narrow public contracts, private internals, owned data/migrations, acyclic dependencies, focused verifiers, and assembled-system evidence.

policies.statement: Every hand-authored textual file in the framework and every generated project starts with a concise format-native description of its current purpose and owning module, surface, or boundary; classes, interfaces, records, structs, enums, and nontrivial public types carry declaration-adjacent responsibility and public-contract or invariant documentation. Preserve shebang, license, and directive order; Markdown documents use meaningful unique referenceable headings, while schemas and comment-free formats use only supported title, description, kind, name, or owner metadata and never invented keys. Renames and ownership or contract changes update these descriptions in the same change, and completed-slice review plus completed-goal and scheduled housekeeping verify their freshness; generated, vendored, lock, and schema-governed artifacts remain generator/schema-owned.
policies.projectionStatement: Every hand-authored textual file has a format-native purpose/owner header and public types have adjacent contract/invariant documentation; preserve required preambles/schema rules and update descriptions with ownership changes. Docs use meaningful unique referenceable headings.

policies.statement: Before every authorized feature, automatically decide from implemented domain language and invariants, data/lifecycle ownership, public contracts, actors and trust/operations, change reason, and dependencies whether it extends an existing module, creates a new module in an existing domain, or establishes a new domain and its first module. Every non-trivial behavior has exactly one active module owner; UI/web, Identity and Access, public API, infrastructure/delivery, and composition remain separate adapting surfaces, generic catch-all placement is invalid, and materially ambiguous placement triggers one focused question plus `$architecture-evolution` before dependent writes.
policies.projectionStatement: Before each feature, use domain invariants, data/lifecycle, contracts, trust/operations, change reason, and dependencies to extend an owner, create a new module in an existing domain, or establish a domain. Every behavior has one owner; ambiguity invokes `$architecture-evolution` rather than a catch-all.

policies.statement: The root Node.js/pnpm/mise toolchain is Codex harness tooling, never a product-stack default. After confirmed manifest requirements and domain placement, select each module's language/framework/runtime from platform/ecosystem, hard/soft real-time latency and jitter, throughput/resources, safety/FFI, data/trust/tenancy, team/tooling, operations, and maintenance evidence; explicitly evaluate Rust and, when deterministic native/hardware/ABI constraints justify its safety cost, C/C++ for real-time/system components. As soon as comparison is meaningful, give one strong primary recommendation with at most one close alternative and explicitly ask the user to confirm, override, or delegate it before implementation. Polyglot choices need a real module/deployment boundary and narrow contracts; actual source/toolchain truth is recorded in `Runtime and technology`, `pnpm stack:detect` ignores harness-only evidence, and housekeeping rejects drift.
policies.projectionStatement: The Node.js/pnpm/mise root is harness tooling, not a product default. After requirements/domain placement, strongly recommend and confirm each module's stack from platform, real-time/resources, safety/FFI, trust/tenancy, team and operations evidence; record actual `Runtime and technology`, and let `pnpm stack:detect` ignore harness-only evidence.

policies.statement: As soon as confirmed users and workflows make it meaningful, derive whether the product is web/PWA, installed mobile, installed desktop, CLI/TUI, API/service, worker, library/SDK, embedded/realtime, or a justified combination. If unclear, promptly ask the developer about usage context, devices, install/offline/distribution, OS/hardware/background capabilities, browser/public-link reach, updates, and cross-device movement without requiring platform jargon. Give one strong recommendation with at most one close alternative and ask the user to confirm, override, or delegate it; manifest System Shape distinguishes selected from actually integrated surfaces before technology selection. Every integrated surface has its own explicit interface directory or declared product package, entry/composition boundary, platform adapters, and exposed public contract/client; surfaces never share a generic app root or deep-import one another, and only explicitly owned genuinely common domain/application contracts, view models, and presentation primitives are shared while platform lifecycle, navigation, screens/routes, adapters, assets, and delivery entrypoints remain surface-local. `scripts/verify/path-hygiene.mjs` enforces physical roots, platform-SDK locality, UI concern separation, and no cross-surface imports.
policies.projectionStatement: Derive and confirm web/PWA, mobile, desktop, CLI/TUI, API/service, worker, library/SDK, embedded/realtime, or combined surfaces before stack choice. Each integrated surface has its own interface directory or declared product package and composition/adapters/contracts; `scripts/verify/path-hygiene.mjs` rejects mixed or cross-imported surfaces.

policies.statement: Every product UI assumes mobile, tablet, and desktop unless the user confirms narrower durable scope. Web uses one content-driven responsive architecture across narrow/medium/wide viewports with feature parity, fluid/container reflow, touch/pointer/keyboard/assistive input, zoom/text reflow, orientation/safe-area/dynamic viewport handling, responsive media, and constrained-device performance; user-agent/device-width branches, fixed desktop shells, hover-only tasks, and duplicated device domain flows are invalid. The UI module owns representative experience evidence without delaying the latest Dev deploy, while surface-quality and completed-goal/scheduled housekeeping enforce the portable guard. Confirm a representative coherent new UI direction before broad implementation. Preserve established appearance, navigation and interaction by default; general repository approval is not unsolicited redesign approval. Material visual-language, information-architecture, navigation, central-interaction or design-system changes need focused consent, while in-scope fixes and accessibility corrections within that direction remain autonomous. Record only confirmed durable UX decisions in existing owners. The implementation skill owns actual rendered-flow and appropriate before/after evidence, with shared-consumer review; source/static/mocked evidence does not prove rendered quality, consent or an unobserved target. Add no UX registry or mandatory screenshot infrastructure. The read-only $ui-ux-review skill owns experience, state, accessibility, design-preservation and shared-consumer review after relevant UI work; it grants no redesign authority. Framework-only work without an affected UI does not trigger it.
policies.projectionStatement: Every UI assumes mobile, tablet, and desktop unless scope is narrowed. Web keeps one responsive feature-parity flow across viewport, input, zoom, orientation, media, and constrained-device conditions; evidence never delays the latest Dev deploy. Confirm new UI direction early; preserve existing design/navigation unless a material change is approved. Use real rendered flows and shared-consumer review, not scanner-based UX claims. Use the read-only $ui-ux-review for affected interactive flows and states; it grants no redesign authority.

policies.statement: Source code, identifiers, filenames, tests, and technical source/declaration headers are always English. During creation and the first definition intake—before surface and stack choices harden—ask whether user-facing UI, public content/metadata, emails/notifications, support, and legal text are single- or multi-locale, then confirm default, supported, and fallback locales plus locale-sensitive formatting and translation ownership when relevant. Every generated child keeps this decision in project-owned `config/localization.json` and manifest truth; `pending` is valid only before product implementation. User-facing language changes use `$native-language-content-review`, and `pnpm localization:check` runs through setup, completed-goal, and scheduled housekeeping.
policies.projectionStatement: Source code and technical headers stay English. Confirm single/multi-locale user content early in project-owned `config/localization.json`; pending ends before product code, and changes use `$native-language-content-review` plus `pnpm localization:check`.

policies.statement: Material changes to product purpose, domain model, system shape, module boundaries, ownership, UI or web surfaces, Identity and Access, public APIs, or infrastructure invoke `$architecture-evolution` for an architecture and repository-layout reassessment; reshape stale files and keep UI/presentation, Identity and Access, public API contracts and transport, domain code, and infrastructure in explicit separately owned roots and internal code boundaries instead of extending an obsolete or mixed structure.
policies.projectionStatement: Material product/domain/system/module/surface changes invoke `$architecture-evolution` and reshape stale files. Keep UI/presentation, Identity and Access, public API contracts/transport, domain code, and infrastructure in explicit separate ownership.

policies.statement: Every completed non-trivial implementation, architecture, configuration-boundary, or integration slice invokes `$system-coherence` before acceptance: inspect the change through current manifest/module ownership, real consumers, and a representative assembled flow; search for competing sources of truth, semantic duplication, misplaced behavior, leaking contracts, dependency/layout drift, and locally clean code that harms the system; then repair material findings at the canonical owner and remove superseded paths. Intentional duplication must have distinct semantics and ownership, while a material topology or migration finding invokes `$architecture-evolution`. In Dev this work runs in a disjoint parallel lane or after the newest developer deploy, never ahead of that feedback loop, but it must finish before the slice becomes a stable dependency or staging/prod input. The same skill owns code-quality review: correctness, naming, error/resource handling, local conventions, maintainability and risk-based regression evidence. Explicit review/diagnosis stays read-only; repair requires an already-authorized implementation scope. Task quality coordinates acceptance without another code-pattern workflow.
policies.projectionStatement: Every non-trivial completed slice invokes `$system-coherence`: inspect a representative assembled flow and real consumers for semantic duplication, competing truth, misplaced ownership, leaking contracts, and structural drift, then repair the canonical owner. Run beside/after the newest developer deploy, but before acceptance or promotion. It also owns code-quality review; review-only requests never authorize edits.

policies.statement: Identity and Access is a dedicated trust and domain boundary: authentication and credentials/authenticators, authorization and server-side policy decisions, principal/account lifecycle and user management, sessions/tokens, audit/persistence, and identity-provider adapters have separate internal owners behind narrow public ports. UI, web, public APIs, product domains, and infrastructure never own or deep-import provider, credential, grant, or session internals; provider settings have one typed environment-aware owner with separate secrets and no product-brand fallback; every material Auth change invokes both `$architecture-evolution` and `$security-review`, with `pnpm auth:check` as its portable structural guard.
policies.projectionStatement: Identity and Access separately owns authentication, authorization, user management, sessions/tokens, audit/persistence, and provider adapters behind public ports. UI/web/public APIs/domains/infrastructure do not own its internals; Auth changes invoke `$architecture-evolution`, `$security-review`, and `pnpm auth:check`.

policies.statement: Every generated project is tenant-capable from creation through visible project-owned `config/tenancy.json`; pending resolution is valid only before product implementation. The first product slice establishes trusted tenant-context resolution, deny-by-default isolation policy, and narrow public ports; principal, verified tenant membership, action, and resource are authorized together, while data/uniqueness/migrations, cache/files/search, messages/jobs, quotas, observability, integrations, and lifecycle stay tenant-scoped. Global or cross-tenant control-plane behavior requires a separate explicit audited capability with no default tenant. Every active module records its isolation and owns negative cross-tenant lifecycle evidence; material changes invoke `$architecture-evolution` and `$security-review`, and `pnpm tenancy:check` runs directly and through completed-goal and scheduled housekeeping.
policies.projectionStatement: Every child is tenant-capable through `config/tenancy.json`; before product code, add trusted tenant context, deny-by-default isolation, and public ports across Auth, data, caches/files/search, jobs, and operations. No default tenant; modules own negative cross-tenant evidence and `pnpm tenancy:check`.

policies.statement: Every generated product is white-label: `config/product.json` begins as the visible replaceable owner for public identity, brand/theme/assets, public endpoints/contacts, and application IDs, deliberately without a public name or repository/package-name fallback; every other setting has one typed owner at its module or composition boundary with checked-in safe defaults, explicit environment overlays, and separate secrets. CodexRig framework metadata remains inspectable for developers but never enters product-facing runtime, UI, public artifacts, metadata, or deployment output.
policies.projectionStatement: Every generated product is white-label: `config/product.json` owns replaceable public identity without repository/package-name fallback; other settings have typed owners, overlays, and separate secrets. Framework metadata stays inspectable but never product-facing.

policies.statement: CodexRig and every noncommercial generated project retain the unmodified PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0, the exact Required Notice, the Zoran Kikic author credit, and the CodexRig Framework credit as managed portable creation and upgrade inputs. Commercial use requires a separate express written license from Zoran Kikic. CodexRig itself always retains its license and credits; only a separate written commercial license may expressly permit their removal from its specifically licensed generated project, and noncommercial use never permits removal. Developer/source attribution remains separate from white-label product-facing output, and `pnpm license:check` fails closed on drift.
policies.projectionStatement: Retain `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, Zoran Kikic, and CodexRig Framework credits in CodexRig and every noncommercial generated project. Commercial use needs a separate written license; only it may permit credit removal from its specifically licensed generated project, never from CodexRig itself. Keep required source attribution separate from white-label output and run `pnpm license:check`.

policies.statement: Portable Codex sessions default to on-request approval and network-disabled workspace-write. Only an explicitly authorized Dev session launched through the canonical `--yolo` control may use no approvals and danger-full-access; that mode never applies to staging or production, never broadens authority, and is bound into startup attestation.
policies.projectionStatement: Portable Codex sessions default to on-request approval and network-disabled workspace-write; only an explicitly authorized Dev session launched with `--yolo` may use no approvals and danger-full-access, never staging or production.

policies.statement: The primary fully orchestrates delegated work, admits at most four live subagents by default only after a completion-budget check, and requires the global delegated defaults, every role, and every subagent to use the exact same configured GPT Astra model and `ultra` reasoning as the primary; no spawn override may differ, a future Astra-version change updates every intelligence setting atomically, and delegation fails closed if the harness cannot guarantee parity. Tracked root `developer_instructions` in `.codex/config.toml` inject primary orchestration, ownership/provenance, intelligence parity, critical drain, and terminal-handover behavior; its `[agents]` table owns the exact global defaults and ceiling, project-scoped `.codex/agents/*.toml` layers inject bounded role behavior, and validation rejects missing or divergent policy. Role sandbox settings are requested defaults because live parent permission overrides, including YOLO, are reapplied to children. Before any delegated repository tool, every child reports its effective runtime permissions. Read-only roles stop on a broader override. An explicitly selected writer may accept the same primary turn's already-authorized YOLO/danger-full-access override only for its canonical repository root and exact disjoint write set; this grants no new scope, network, credential, external-mutation, commit, push, publication, deployment, or delegation authority. Any other permission mismatch, uncertain provenance, or overlap stops delegated repository work. Every spawn and background process is recorded before use with repository realpath and stable identity, primary session/thread identity, canonical task, scope, returned identity, checkpoint, safe-boundary behavior, and cancellation provenance. Account- or host-wide process listings are untrusted discovery only: the primary acts exclusively on complete registry matches and never contacts or changes foreign or ambiguous processes; this process rule never makes visible same-host project files foreign. Capacity uses the most constraining current host signal without assuming a billing period or unit: a reliable remaining percentage is guarded at 10% or less and critical at 5% or less, an absolute remaining token/credit amount is compared directly with bounded work and completion reserves, any host critical/exhaustion signal or reserve shortfall is critical, and unavailable or unauthorized redeem/reset capacity counts as zero. Monitoring runs before admission/follow-up and after material results, scope changes, long waits, checkpoints, and host warnings, with no more than ten minutes between heartbeats during active delegation unless a known long-running operation has an explicit checkpoint; every slice has Orchestration Housekeeping and every goal has its deep form. Guarded state stops optional delegation, shortens checkpoints, and keeps the single bounded `docs/project-context.md` current. Critical state starts no subagent, task, or slice; it drains every provenance-bound owned agent and process to a safe boundary, records all handoffs, closes them, confirms none remain, and only then seals a resumable handover. Peers may exchange bounded evidence, status, contract implications, readiness, and risk only when the primary supplies their identities and scopes; every direct exchange is mirrored immediately to the primary and never changes delegation, ownership, write authority, integration, or lifecycle control. Within one primary-owned local run, writers may share a checkout only under exact disjoint file ownership that the primary continuously monitors; independent sessions on one developer host use dedicated one-lease worktrees, while different developers/hosts use separate clones plus confirmed shared coordination. Codex account identity changes neither boundary. This is logical/workspace isolation, never a false sandbox or authentication claim. The primary retains integration authority and never permits a subagent to commit, merge, push, publish, deploy, use credentials, or delegate. Every spawn has a task-appropriate checkpoint; the primary audits only its provenance-bound agents at checkpoints, handoffs, new admission, completed-goal housekeeping, and final handoff, accepts or preserves each result, closes completed agents, interrupts idle, blocked, abandoned, or redundant owned agents without a concrete assignment, and informs affected active agents about accepted results, changed contracts or assumptions, remaining work, and released ownership or slots.
policies.projectionStatement: The primary admits at most four live subagents after a completion-budget check; root `developer_instructions`, global delegated defaults, every role, and each subagent enforce primary orchestration plus the exact same configured GPT Astra model and `ultra` reasoning, with no spawn override. Role sandboxes are requested defaults because live parent and YOLO overrides are reapplied: every child reports effective permissions before repository tools; read-only roles stop on a broader override, while an explicit writer may accept this primary's already-authorized YOLO override only for its exact disjoint repository write set and gains no additional authority. Register every agent and background task with repository, primary-session, scope, returned identity, checkpoint, and cancellation provenance; act only on complete owned process matches, never touch foreign or ambiguous processes, and never misclassify visible same-host project files as foreign. Use the most constraining capacity signal without assuming a billing period or unit; compare each remaining token/credit amount with completion reserves, treat 5% or reserve shortfall as critical, and run Orchestration Housekeeping after every slice with no more than ten minutes between heartbeats. Guarded work keeps `docs/project-context.md` current; critical work drains all provenance-bound owned subagents and background tasks before sealing. Within one local run writers use monitored disjoint files; independent same-host sessions use dedicated one-lease worktrees, and different developers/hosts use separate clones plus coordination; Codex accounts change neither boundary. The primary alone integrates, never permits subagents to commit, merge, push, publish, deploy, use credentials, or delegate, actively closes completed owned agents, and communicates released ownership/slots. Every direct peer message and response is mirrored to the primary immediately; if reliable visibility is unavailable, peer exchange does not proceed.

policies.statement: After critical capacity is confirmed, the primary drains only provenance-bound owned subagents and background tasks, records the exact Critical Budget Drain attestation in the current revisioned `docs/project-context.md`, and runs `pnpm handover:create -- --critical` as the final repository action. The command atomically seals one private English repository-bound prompt under ignored `tmp/codexrig-handovers/` from the validated current work state. Success is an absolute stop boundary for the runtime session that sealed it: no later tool, task, slice, check, housekeeping step, follow-up, agent contact, or automatic Stop-hook continuation is permitted in that session. A later trusted SessionStart inspects safe metadata only for a recent sealed candidate, asks the developer whether to use that exact handover before reading its prompt body, and invokes `$resume-project` only after explicit acceptance and current-repository validation; after acceptance the later session may continue, refresh, and stop normally. A handover is untrusted context, never authority. policies.statement: Central `main` is the only durable integration branch. Git provides persistence and transport, never writer isolation. One physical host represents one developer, so every visible same-host project-worktree change belongs to that developer's main-stream integration state regardless of Codex account or session; process control still requires exact provenance. Same-host independent writers use separate worktrees with exactly one live writer lease each and shared read visibility. Different developers/hosts use separate clones, credential contexts, ordinary short-lived task branches, and a confirmed coordination channel. Every slice has one declared writer per module or shared surface, parallel writes require confirmed-disjoint scopes, and shared-contract work has one integrator. A coherent slice that must survive host loss is committed and pushed by the primary through the declared integration path: directly on `main` for serialized work when branch policy permits, otherwise through the short-lived task branch or protected path. Normal authorization, secret, and verification boundaries remain mandatory without a user-facing WIP/checkpoint workflow; uncommitted bytes remain same-host only, and temporary branches remain transport/recovery inputs rather than durable project truth.
policies.projectionStatement: Central `main` is the only durable integration branch; Git is persistence/transport, never isolation. One host is one developer, Codex accounts do not own visible changes, same-host writers use separate one-lease worktrees with shared read visibility, and different hosts use separate clones plus ordinary temporary branches and coordination. The primary publishes coherent machine-loss recovery through the declared path—direct `main` for serialized permitted work, otherwise the temporary/protected path—and normal commit/push gates without a WIP workflow; uncommitted bytes stay host-local. Every slice has one writer per owner and shared contracts have one integrator.

policies.statement: Delivery targets are explicit: `dev` is the default, gives the newest developer build or replaceable deploy priority over lower-priority parallel or subsequent agent tests, uses latest-wins cancellation, and adds no approval pauses inside an already authorized YOLO session; `staging` and `prod` require explicit selection and progressively stronger gates. Generated projects keep declared and repository-detected integrated environments in project-owned `config/delivery.json` without treating the Dev default as proof that a deployment exists. Stronger-target repository evidence requires a clean current commit, a real ignored `.delivery/` manifest whose target, source commit, sorted artifact files and non-secret configuration files are rehashed from actual bytes and modes, and a project-owned `verify:staging` or `verify:prod` command executed after repository/build/test checks; caller-asserted digests are forbidden, and artifact, configuration, or target-plan drift invalidates evidence.
policies.projectionStatement: Delivery is explicit: `dev` is the default; the newest developer build/deploy wins over parallel or later tests and an already authorized YOLO session adds no approval pauses. Staging/prod require explicit stronger gates; `config/delivery.json` separates selected default from real integrated targets. Stronger evidence uses a clean commit, an actual rehashed `.delivery/` artifact/config manifest, and the project-owned target verifier—never a caller-asserted digest.

policies.statement: Housekeeping has two explicit layers: primary-owned Orchestration Housekeeping observes host capacity, provenance-bound owned processes, checkpoints, handoffs, ownership, bounded work state, every same-clone worktree, and shared coordination on material events and after every slice; repository-only `repo:housekeeping` can observe none of the host conversation/process graph. After every completed slice the lightweight read-only Worktree Settlement trigger reruns `worktree:status -- --json` and rechecks session, lease, recovery, task-branch, handover, prune-transaction, reservation, and preservation-lock claims. Preservation is a safety state, never completion: every no-longer-needed item is integrated, kept under a named live owner and scope, explicitly owner-confirmed and repaired or retired, mechanically retired only when proven stale or missing under the current contract, or retained with a concrete blocker and resolution condition. A clean or integrated temporary worktree remains unsettled when it is no longer needed. Every completed goal runs the deep orchestration layer and then one primary-owned `repo:housekeeping --apply` reconciliation before its goal-wide documentation review, final audit, verification, and publication; the goal stays open until every no-longer-needed goal-owned worktree, branch, writer/session claim, handover, transaction, lock/reservation, and generated/process residue is retired, while the current owning session may remain only until its mandatory post-exit reset. Normal terminal release and stale cleanup repair a missing or invalid recovery marker from the exact active-phase lease before removing it while retaining any different valid latest marker. Apply mode accepts a Git-less project root and removes only mechanically proven stale coordination state; a current process identity observed outside its bound PID namespace or otherwise mechanically indeterminate remains an ownership-confirmation blocker. Missing or unobservable Linux procfs is likewise indeterminate. An existing directory with a broken Git worktree link is preserved instead of repaired automatically. Metadata-only pruning removes only missing registrations whose paths remain held by exact process-bound non-directory reservations across the native prune, while process-bound Git locks protect every non-missing linked sibling. Before native prune, one shared process-bound transaction in the Git common directory records every reserved path and preservation reason, so interrupted cleanup remains discoverable after Git removes a registration; a failed or identity-changed reservation leaves its registration intact. After an interrupted cleanup, only an unchanged current-contract transaction, reservation, or preservation lock whose exact owner is mechanically proven dead is retired automatically. Only after the primary or developer confirms that a directory still belongs to its registration may the primary run an explicit native Git repair and resume housekeeping. Inventory continues across per-root inconsistencies. Every actual active, dirty, unintegrated, unsafe, invalid, or ambiguous worktree is preserved as developer-owned main-stream input and blocks only affected unsafe writes or closure for primary reconciliation; repository housekeeping never removes an actual worktree directory. A safely readable invalid orphan recovery file without usable writer evidence remains preserved and visible as an advisory instead of blocking independent work. In the reusable source framework the command also queries the configured central remote branch read-only, requires its unique live commit to equal the local tracking ref, classifies active changes against that immutable publication baseline with conservative SemVer impact, and transactionally synchronizes `.codexrig/framework.json`, `package.json`, and the bounded manifest version block through a crash-recoverable journal; generated products retain an independent product/package version and record their installed framework version only in `.codexrig/installation.json`. The command updates only unambiguous repository facts such as detected delivery inventory and its bounded manifest projection, then checks architecture, docs and source headers, tenant/Auth/surface/white-label boundaries, dependencies, secrets, tool/model policy, and framework health without deploying, committing, pushing, or mutating external environments. Ambiguous evidence fails closed; scheduled CI runs the read-only online check.

After every completed slice its read-only Worktree Settlement trigger reruns `worktree:status -- --json` and session, lease, recovery, task-branch, handover, transaction, reservation, and preservation-lock claims. Preservation is a safety state, never completion: every no-longer-needed item reaches an explicit terminal disposition or retains a concrete blocker and resolution condition, and a clean or integrated temporary worktree remains unsettled while no longer needed. A completed goal stays open until every no-longer-needed goal-owned worktree and related coordination residue is retired; the current owning session remains only until mandatory post-exit reset. Normal release and stale cleanup repair missing or invalid recovery from the exact active-phase lease before removing it and retain any valid latest marker. A current identity observed outside its bound PID namespace or otherwise indeterminate remains an ownership-confirmation blocker; missing or unobservable Linux procfs is also indeterminate. It preserves existing directories with broken Git worktree links. It prunes only missing registrations whose paths remain held by exact process-bound non-directory reservations across the native prune while process-bound Git locks protect every non-missing linked sibling. A shared process-bound Git-common transaction records every reserved path and preservation reason before prune, so post-prune crashes remain discoverable; a failed or changed reservation leaves its registration intact. After an interrupted cleanup, only unchanged current-contract artifacts with a proven-dead exact owner are retired automatically. Native Git repair is explicit and primary-owned after ownership confirmation. Per-root inconsistencies remain visible while safe independent recovery continues; every actual active, dirty, unintegrated, unsafe, invalid, or ambiguous worktree is preserved, while orphan recovery corruption without unsafe writer ownership remains advisory. In CodexRig source it also transactionally reconciles SemVer from the verified central publication baseline. It never removes an actual worktree, deploys, commits, pushes, or mutates external state.

policies.statement: Complex work uses reviewable slices, focused changed-path evidence, review and repair to zero relevant findings, a fresh audit, whole-repository course checks, and one final verification on the actual integration state; environment-specific evidence never promotes to a stronger target implicitly. Additional evidence must address an approved outcome, acceptance blocker or material risk. Material behavior corrections first reproduce the original failing regression with a concise problem/contract header in an existing suite; editorial changes need no mirrored tests. Text-presence checks prove required policy/routing, not semantic consistency, native delivery or model compliance; mocks, rendered targets and actual account-backed behavior retain distinct evidence.

Keep evidence risk-proportionate; distinguish policy presence, mocks, native delivery, rendered behavior and actual account-backed observations.

policies.statement: Never end at "ready to implement" when implementation is already authorized. Plans, research, recaps, gates, reviews, audits, and readiness statements are intermediate; continue through the complete outcome and published goal checkpoints until a real authority, safety, integration, or external blocker remains. Approvals persist within confirmed scope; additive main-stream questions, status requests and constraints are answered or incorporated before returning to the active outcome. Explicit pause, cancellation or replacement changes the mandate, and side conversations remain independent unless brought into the main stream. General improvement mandates authorize no speculative features or unsolicited redesign. Ask only decision-relevant questions after safe concrete preparation; explain skill-caused pauses, preserving higher-priority constraints. Native Codex owns Goals, plans, sessions and work controls; Goals require explicit request and no invented budget. pnpm goal:new is a publication check, not a Goal creator. Preserve current Stop protection until the native installed path proves continuation, pause/cancellation, side-conversation, recovery and terminal-handover replacement. Required reset/publication leaves closure open, not falsely complete; create no second task runtime.
policies.projectionStatement: Never end at "ready to implement" when implementation is already authorized. Plans, research, reviews, audits, and goals are intermediate until the complete outcome or a real blocker. Existing approvals persist in scope; additive questions return to the active outcome, explicit pause/cancel/replacement is honored. Use explicitly requested native Goals, without a second runtime or false completion at reset/publication boundaries.

policies.statement: Framework upgrades accept only the current framework-contract, installation-receipt, and policy-projection schemas, update managed capabilities transactionally, and reconcile versioned policy concepts into each child's local truth. They reject non-current installations, never copy project-owned documents blindly, and never invent active product modules; a non-current child must be regenerated from the current framework.

Older installations are regenerated rather than interpreted; project-owned documents are never blindly copied and active modules are never invented.

policies.statement: `.codexrig/` owns versioned framework, compatibility, installation, managed-surface, provider, and upgrade contracts; only reviewed sources may update a child, and every update is previewed, receipt-backed, transactional, and verified after local reconciliation.
policies.projectionStatement: `.codexrig/` owns versioned framework/compatibility/upgrade contracts; only reviewed sources update children through previewed, receipt-backed transactions followed by local reconciliation and verification.

policies.statement: The reusable CodexRig source has one stable SemVer owner in `.codexrig/framework.json`, mirrored exactly in root `package.json` and the bounded source-manifest version block. Completed-goal `repo:housekeeping --apply` resolves the configured central-main remote and branch, reads its unique live commit, requires the local remote-tracking ref to match it exactly and remain an ancestor of local `HEAD`, and classifies every unpublished commit plus active tracked and untracked change against that immutable publication baseline: removals or incompatible contract/policy/managed-surface changes require major, behavior/capability/policy changes require minor, and documentation/test-only changes require patch; it selects at least the required next version without downgrading an explicit higher valid release and transactionally writes all mirrors through crash-recoverable state. Missing, stale, or ambiguous remote/upstream identity fails closed. Repeated runs are idempotent, read-only and scheduled checks fail on drift, and a functional source release can never reuse its published version. Generated projects keep their independent product/package version; `.codexrig/installation.json` alone records which framework version they installed, and framework upgrades never overwrite product versioning.
policies.projectionStatement: CodexRig source owns one stable SemVer in `.codexrig/framework.json`, transactionally mirrored to root package metadata and its source manifest by completed-goal housekeeping from the unique live configured central-remote commit, which must match the local tracking ref, through crash-recoverable state; breaking/behavior/docs-only changes require major/minor/patch and reruns are idempotent. Generated products keep an independent product version; `.codexrig/installation.json` records their installed framework version.

policies.statement: Framework behavior is inspectable: portable policy, roles, skills, hooks, managed files, exclusions, and upgrade actions are tracked and documented; only explicitly documented sensitive or disposable runtime state is ignored, never normative project policy.
